children: beat Wall Street's quarterly sales and earnings estimates on Tuesday and said it now expects full-year sales growth at the top of its prior forecast. Shares fell about 2% in premarket trading as the retailer projected an adjusted operating margin at the low end of its previous range.

Third-quarter revenue rose 4.9% to $43.4 billion, ahead of the $42.8 billion analysts expected, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. Adjusted earnings rose to $3.86 per share from $3.74 a year earlier, edging past the $3.84 estimate. Comparable sales climbed 2.2% both globally and in the U.S., where they had risen 1.3% the previous quarter.

Home Depot now expects fiscal 2026 sales to grow about 4.5%, compared with its previous range of 2.5% to 4.5%. It sees adjusted earnings per share rising about 2%, the midpoint of its earlier forecast, and expects an adjusted operating margin of about 12.8%, the bottom of its prior range.
The retailer also named finance chief Richard McPhail as its next CEO, effective Nov. 23. He succeeds Ted Decker, who will remain board chair.

Demand from professional contractors has held up better than spending by do-it-yourself customers, while high borrowing costs continue to weigh on bigger renovation projects. McPhail helped oversee Home Depot's expansion into contractor supplies, including its acquisitions of SRS Distribution and GMS. The next test for investors is whether that business can keep comparable sales growing while improving margins, especially if homeowners continue putting off larger projects.

title: Home Depot's Earnings Beat Wasn't Enough for Investors
